summary: Addressing class imbalance improves model quality when measured by discriminative threshold-dependent metrics. F1-score improved by +2.93% on average across all models, and balanced accuracy by +5.22%, indicating that balanced weighting successfully optimizes for recall on the minority class. However, ROC-AUC (which is inherently robust to class imbalance) showed negligible change (-0.0018%), demonstrating that the improvement is in the decision threshold, not discriminative capacity.
direction: Imbalance handling improves F1-score and balanced accuracy, not ROC-AUC
methodological_choices: Train-test split (70-30, stratified to preserve class distribution). Preprocessing: removed rows with missing values, label-encoded 8 categorical features, standardized 6 numeric features. Three model families tested: Logistic Regression, Random Forest (100 estimators), Gradient Boosting (100 estimators). Imbalance handling via class_weight='balanced' (LR, RF) and sample_weight in fit (GB). Evaluation metrics: ROC-AUC, F1, balanced accuracy, precision, recall. No hyperparameter tuning. Dataset: 48,842 rows, 3.18:1 class imbalance ratio (76% negative, 24% positive).
